nh_sundown_bouldering.blurb: Sundown Bouldering is a boulder field in Albany, New Hampshire, along the Kancamagus Highway in the White Mountains. The blocks are arranged in tiers and clusters, among them Tier 1 Left Side, Tier 3, the Main Cliff Boulders in the talus below the cliff, and the Campground Boulders. It is all bouldering, with a steady spread from V0 up to V10 and the heaviest concentration in the middle grades. The approaches to the main groups are short and easy, the river is near the parking, and the swimming holes are a walk away, which suits a mixed group. Many blocks have seen few ascents, so expect some brushing, and a spotter or a step ladder helps on newer problems.

az_jacks_canyon.blurb: Jacks Canyon is a sport climbing area in a scenic canyon in northern Arizona, north of Winslow. The routes are almost all bolted, on limestone with pockets and edges, and the bolting is generous. Grades start in the 5.5 to 5.9 range and top out above 5.13, but the bulk sits between 5.10 and 5.12, so strong intermediate and advanced climbers have the most to choose from. The main sections are Cracker Jack Cliffs, Main Wall, Casino Cliffs and High Life Wall, and most approaches are short walks. Much of the canyon is shaded, so you can follow the sun or shade through the year. March to May and September to November are the best windows.

co_morrison_boulders.blurb: Morrison Boulders is a long-standing Front Range bouldering area on the hogback ridge at the edge of the foothills, close to Denver. The rock is hard sandstone, and the problems lean toward greasy slopers with some sharp crimps, polished by heavy use. The climbing is almost entirely bouldering across a wide range, from V0 to a thin tail of very hard problems, with many solid problems in the V1 to V5 range and a reputation for strong, steep climbing at the top end. The Black Hole and the Lobby sit on the north side of town and are good on sunny winter days, while the Dark Side, across the road to the south, is a slope of tall angular blocks. It is busy and sociable, and climbable much of the year.

nh_bayle_mountain_bouldering.blurb: Bayle Mountain Bouldering lies in Ossipee, in New Hampshire's Lakes Region, on a mountain that forms part of an ancient circular ring of volcanic intrusion. The stone is unusual and very rough: coarse quartz syenite, with some pink granite and rhyolite, so bring tough skin. Large erratics are spread through thick woods in a series of small groups, among them the Culvert, Forbidding, Entrance and Skatepark boulders. Everything is bouldering, mostly V1 to V5 with a smaller number of harder problems up to V7. It makes for a fine day of exploring rather than a destination trip, and the bugs can be severe in the thick forest.
